CITY of ALBUQUERQUE 
TWENTY-FIRST COUNCIL 
 
 
COUNCIL BILL NO.       R-14-113                   ENACTMENT NO.   ________________________ 
 
SPONSORED BY:  
Don Harris 
 
 
RESOLUTION 
1 
RECOGNIZING THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THE HISTORIC SITE ADJACENT TO 
2 
THE SINGING ARROW COMMUNITY CENTER, KNOWN AS RANCHO DE 
3 
CARNUÉ, IN ORDER TO RECOGNIZE AND PRESERVE THE 
4 
ARCHAEOLOGICAL AND CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE OF THE SITE, AND 
5 
DESIGNATE IT WORTHY OF ADDITIONAL ARCHAEOLOGICAL 
6 
INVESTIGATIONS, PRESERVATION, AND INTERPRETATION; MAKING AN 
7 
APPROPRIATION TO THE OPEN SPACE DIVISION OF THE PARKS AND 
8 
RECREATION DEPARTMENT 
9 
WHEREAS, settlement of the Tijeras Canyon area is of great historical 
10 
importance to the history of Albuquerque and surrounding traditional 
11 
communities such as the Cañón de Carnué land grant and Isleta Pueblo; and 
12 
WHEREAS, evidence of this settlement is found in numerous 
13 
archaeological and historic sites along the Tijeras Arroyo; and 
14 
WHEREAS, the archaeological site of Rancho de Carnué was donated to 
15 
the City of Albuquerque for the preservation and protection of its land and 
16 
location; and 
17 
WHEREAS, archaeological investigations conducted at Rancho de Carnué 
18 
were done over 35 years ago and since then the site adjacent to the Singing 
19 
Arrow community has been protected but undeveloped; and 
20 
WHEREAS, new techniques are available to re-examine the site so that 
21 
more of the site area can be used for interpretation, education, and more 
22 
active public access; and  
23 
WHEREAS, such investigation and site re-design will enhance the site’s 
24 
historic character and quality of life for all of the City’s residents. 
25

BE IT RESOLVED, BY THE COUNCIL THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF

ALBUQUERQUE: 
2 
 
Section 1. That the archaeological site adjacent to the Singing Arrow 
3 
Community Center, known as Rancho de Carnué, is both historically and 
4 
culturally important to the community, and to designate the site worthy of 
5 
additional archeological investigations, preservation, and redevelopment for 
6 
the citizens of Albuquerque. 
7 
 
Section 2. That up to Seventy Five Thousand Dollars ($75,000) is hereby 
8 
designated within the City Council Projects activity for the purpose of funding 
9 
archeological investigations, interpretation, site design, and related activities 
10 
of Rancho de Carnué adjacent to the Singing Arrow Community.

CITY of ALBUQUERQUE 
TWENTY-FIRST COUNCIL 
 
 
COUNCIL BILL NO.        R-14-82                 ENACTMENT NO.   ________________________ 
 
SPONSORED BY: 
Don Harris 
 
 
RESOLUTION 
1 
FOR AN AREA OF APPROXIMATELY 684 ACRES, THAT INCLUDES THE 
2 
TIJERAS CANYON AND THE TIJERAS ARROYO FOR APPROXIMATELY 3.7 
3 
MILES FROM THE CARÑUEL INTERSTATE-40 INTERCHANGE WESTWARD TO 
4 
THE BOUNDARY OF KIRTLAND AIR FORCE BASE; ADOPTING THE 
5 
RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PLAN FOR THE TIJERAS ARROYO BIOLOGICAL 
6 
ZONE (RMP FOR THE TABZ) AS A RANK II FACILITY PLAN. 
7 
 
WHEREAS, the City Council, the governing body of the City of 
8 
Albuquerque, has the authority to adopt and amend plans for the physical 
9 
development of areas within the planning and platting jurisdiction of the City 
10 
authorized by Statute, Section 3-19-1 et. Seq., NMSA 1978, and by its home rule 
11 
powers; and 
12 
 
WHEREAS, approval of the RMP for the TABZ is consistent with the 
13 
applicable goals and policies of the Albuquerque/Bernalillo County 
14 
Comprehensive Plan, the Major Open Space Facility Plan, the Facility Plan for 
15 
Arroyos, and the East Gateway Sector Development Plan; and 
16 
     WHEREAS, The Facility Plan for Arroyos, adopted in 1986, calls for the 
17 
entirety of the 100-year floodplains of Major Open Space Arroyos to be 
18 
purchased by the City as open space and remain in a natural or semi-natural 
19 
condition, and the Plan designates the portion of Tijeras Arroyo from the 
20 
eastern city limits to Kirtland AFB on the west as a Major Open Space Arroyo; 
21 
and 
22 
     WHEREAS, The Albuquerque/Bernalillo County Major Public Open Space 
23 
Facility Plan, adopted in 1999, specifically calls for a Resource Management 
24 
Plan to be developed for the Tijeras Arroyo; and 
25

land acquisition for open space— will help to curb inappropriate development 
1 
in the floodplain and valley areas where flood danger, high water table, and 
2 
soils inhibit extensive urbanization.   
3 
 
c. Developing and Established Urban Area Policies 
4 
The request is consistent with the Developing and Established Urban Area 
5 
Goal and furthers Policy II.B.5.d because  approval and implementation of the 
6 
RMP for the TABZ will help ensure that new development respects existing 
7 
natural environmental conditions and carrying capacities, scenic resources, 
8 
and cultural and recreational resources by listing and describing those 
9 
conditions and resources in detail and providing policies and best practices 
10 
for managing them.   
11 
 
d. Archaeological Resource Policies 
12 
The request is consistent with the Archaeological Resource Goal and 
13 
furthers Policies II.C.6.a, b and c because the Plan surveys and evaluates the 
14 
significance of several archaeological and paleontological sites and presents 
15 
strategies for preserving and managing them for research and education.   
16 
The request furthers Policy II.C.8.a because the RMP for the TABZ 
17 
inventories important visual and environmental resources unique to the 
18 
Tijeras Arroyo floodplain and notes their significance, facilitating their being 
19 
taken into account in development decisions. 
20 
 
e. Water Management Policies 
21 
The request is consistent with the Water Management Goal and furthers 
22 
Policy II.D.2.b because the RMP for the TABZ policies encourage the 
23 
maximum absorption of precipitation through the retention of the natural 
24 
arroyo (the Tijeras Arroyo) and conservation of run-off within the context of 
25 
overall water resource management.    
26 
 
f. Education Policies 
27 
The request is consistent with the Education Goal and furthers Policy 
28 
II.D.7.d
